meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) International Company Register
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: English Common Law heritage (inherited through New Zealand trusteeship) with customary law overlay under the Constitution of the Independent State of Samoa 1960
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (Apostille Convention, in force for Samoa)
PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, effective 2020)

International Companies Amendment Act 2020); International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2018; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (as amended); Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Prevention) Regulations 2015; SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines for Licensed Registered Agents; Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) directives under the Central Bank of Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified color copy of UBO passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if country of origin is a Contracting State; otherwise Consular Legalization at a Samoan diplomatic/consular post or reciprocal consular arrangement

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in country of origin; Apostille or Consular Legalization as required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference / banker's conformity letter confirming account conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Referencing bank of UBO or corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, and Samoa FIU domestic designations; PEP identification covering foreign, domestic, and international-organization PEPs with enhanced due diligence for higher-risk relationships, applying FATF Recommendation 12; risk-based verification through SIFA-licensed registered agent using independent electronic databases; adverse-media and negative-news check required for UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories of the International Company.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — Registrar of International Companies; name clearance submitted via licensed SIFA Registered Agent (online portal and e-mail filing channel)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official languages of Samoa are Samoan and English; the corporate name must be in Latin script and contain a statutory suffix such as 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Pty Limited', or 'Ltd'; Chinese-language business names are permitted only as a transliterated Latin-script trade name (pinyin or English equivalent), with the Chinese character rendering recorded in the agent's internal localization file but not on the Certificate of Incorporation; prohibited names include any name identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered Samoan or international company, names that imply governmental, royal, or sovereign patronage, and names containing obscene or offensive matter.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant through its licensed registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating grounds of distinctiveness and supporting evidence; the Registrar issues a final administrative determination within 15 business days; a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Samoa under Part 2 of the International Companies Act 2005; name reservation extensions must be lodged via the registered agent before expiry of the 30-day window, with each extension ordinarily granted for an additional 30-day period at the Registrar's discretion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the statutory registered office: a physical Samoan registered office maintained by a SIFA-licensed registered agent is mandatory for an International Company; however, a virtual/remote principal place of business is acceptable for the localization agency's operational headquarters since the company is foreign-managed and non-resident-owner oriented; Samoa's economic substance requirements for International Companies post-2020 are satisfied by adequate expenditure, premises, and employees or, for purely foreign-source service income, by demonstrating that core income-generating activities are carried on outside Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 2–5% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months for a low-risk professional translation/localization entity; SIFA primarily conducts annual desk-based AML compliance reviews of registered agents and targeted physical inspections only where material compliance deficiencies, sanctions matches, or suspicious transaction reports are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2019 (Samoa), Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 7-14; International Companies Regulations 2019 (prescribed forms and fee schedule); Business Registration Act 2015 (optional onshore activity).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) - Corporate Registry, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form 1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and Consent to Act as Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; incorporation is permitted with a single share of any par or no-par value. No escrow account or capital deposit is required; subscription consideration is declared fully paid on allotment. Authorized capital determines the SIFSA registration fee band.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST, that the allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares at US$1 par value each, to the initial subscriber named in the Memorandum and Articles of Association, be and is hereby approved, and the subscription consideration is declared fully paid. RESOLVED SECOND, that the registered office situated in Apia, Samoa, as specified in the registered agent's consent, be and is hereby adopted as the Company's registered office. RESOLVED THIRD, that [NAME] be appointed as sole Director, and [NAME] as Company Secretary, each holding office until removal or resignation, and be authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts binding the Company, instruct the Registered Agent, and perform all acts necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Corporate Registry through a licensed Samoa Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed company names to the licensed registered agent, who checks the SIFSA name index for identical or deceptively similar names. Upon clearance, the name is reserved for 30 days. The name must end with 'Limited' or an approved suffix and must not contain restricted words such as Bank, Trust, or Insurance without regulatory consent.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name list (up to three options)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or restricted words, substitute one of the alternative names; a written objection may be lodged with SIFSA for reconsideration within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutive Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoa Registered Agent and the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, or bilingual Chinese/English custom articles, compliant with the International Companies Act 2019. Execute all instruments before a witness, and arrange notarization or certification of identity documents for each shareholder and director.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to Act as Registered Agent
Certified passport copies of shareholders and directors
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank reference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficient certifications and re-execute the affected pages; the registered agent coordinates rectification without requiring full re-notarization where the Act permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Application for Incorporation (Form 1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, Consent to Act as Registered Agent, and the prescribed filing fee of approximately US$500. Payment is remitted through the registered agent's client account, and SIFSA conducts its statutory compliance review.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFSA issues a requisition or deficiency letter, respond within 14 days by amending the documents and re-filing corrected pages; unresolved objections may be appealed to the Registrar under the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, SIFSA issues the Certificate of Incorporation and certified extracts. The registered agent retrieves the certificate and conducts an internal completeness review against the approved constitutive documents.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply for a replacement certificate upon proof of loss; request administrative correction through the registered agent if the name, date, or capital details on the certificate are erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution adopting the pro forma resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and appointment of directors and secretary. Signed minutes must be retained in the company register maintained by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution or written consent
Appointment forms for directors and secretary
Consent to act of each appointed officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer declines appointment, execute a replacement consent and update the company registers within 10 days; any change is filed with the registered agent for registry annotation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent, corporate banks (Wise Business, Payoneer), and SIFSA annual compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation and the first board resolution. Arrange SIFSA annual license fee payments. If a physical onshore office is intended, register under the Business Registration Act 2015 with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Bank account queries are resolved via updated corporate registers or a re-issued board resolution; any missing due-diligence documents must be produced within 10 business days to avoid account suspension.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for offshore International Company operations; translation and media dubbing constitute a non-regulated knowledge service. For any onshore physical office, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) administers registration under the Business Registration Act 2015.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for offshore activities; optional Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Act 2015 for a physical onshore office in Samoa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment; office-based operations fall under low-impact development (Category 4) and require only a building and occupancy permit under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2014, not a formal Environmental Impact Statement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to office-only premises; minimum compliance with the Waste Management Act 2011 for office waste disposal, the Water Resources Management Act 2009 for sanitary sewer connection, and applicable indoor air quality thresholds for office HVAC systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Applicable only where a physical onshore office exists: fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); structural occupancy clearance from the Building Inspectorate of the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI) under the Building Code of Samoa; electrical safety certificate from the Electrical Inspectorate. For a purely offshore operation without premises, no clearance is triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry of Revenue; official e-services portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws (SRA e-Tax Portal for TIN registration, VAGST filings, and certificates).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) is incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 with the Registrar of International Companies at the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). SIFA transmits incorporation data to the SRA for automatic issuance of a Tax Identification Number (TIN). Alternatively, the IC may file a direct TIN application form (Form TIN-01) with the SRA, submitting certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, directors'/shareholders' register, and a registered agent's undertaking in Samoa. The TIN is typically issued within 2-5 business days. The IC is not required to obtain a VAGST registration number if its activities are confined to offshore commercial activity outside Samoa; however, local banking, payroll, or administrative presence may require TIN enrollment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. The IC receives statutory exemption from Samoa income tax, income tax on distributions, VAGST, and stamp duty in respect of all international business activities, contracts, and transactions entered into outside Samoa. Such exemption applies as long as the IC does not carry on business with Samoan residents or own Samoan land, and no beneficial interest in the IC is held by a Samoan resident.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' entity classification election exists in Samoa (no pass-through election into the ordinary tax regime is permitted for an IC). Elections are limited to (i) the constitutional election to issue shares with or without par value, (ii) dividend declaration elections under the International Companies Act which are tax-exempt, and (iii) the election to apply Samoa's exchange control or the International Companies (Foreign Exchange) Exemption order for foreign currency transactions; hybrid mismatch treatments under the Tax Administration Act 2012 are unavailable to ICs because the entity is wholly tax-transparent in Samoa by virtue of its statutory exemption, so no anti-hybrid or CFC inclusion arises at the Samoan domestic level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_narrative: For a definitive exclusion from Samoan tax, the IC must file a declaration of exempt status with the SRA upon request, supported by a certificate from the Registrar confirming offshore-only operations; the IC may also elect in its constitution to rely on the full exemption in Section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987, including exemption from exchange control (with annual reporting to the Central Bank of Samoa where applicable).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the VAGST Act 1998 (as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 per annum (registration is mandatory when annual taxable turnover exceeds WST 100,000). An International Company carrying on exclusively offshore business in multilingual localization is statutorily exempt and outside the VAGST registration net; if the IC were to make any taxable supplies within Samoa (e.g., local studio rental or domestic post-production), the WST 100,000 threshold would apply and VAGST would be chargeable on that domestic portion only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based pre-clearance regime is currently enacted in Samoa. The SRA operates a post-audit compliance model; registered persons must issue tax invoices in a prescribed format containing supplier name/TIN, buyer details, description, supplier and buyer VAGST registration numbers, date, consideration, and VAGST amount (shown separately). E-invoicing is voluntary, but the SRA encourages electronic records; non-resident IC exporters should maintain all invoices, delivery dockets, and digital service delivery logs electronically to substantiate zero-rated export treatment. The SRA may require electronic filing of VAGST returns and attachment of invoice summaries; no third-party clearance provider is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of services are zero-rated under Section 7 and Schedule 2 of the VAGST Act 1998 where the services are supplied to a recipient who is a non-resident, are exported or consumed outside Samoa, and the supplier retains documentary evidence of the offshore delivery. Multilingual translation, localization, dubbing, and media transcription services rendered to offshore clients (non-resident agencies, studios, or content platforms) qualify for 0% VAT provided the IC does not itself perform the work from a physical Samoan studio used for domestic supplies and does not supply to a Samosan resident. Services must not be in connection with land or goods situated in Samoa at the time of supply. The IC should obtain a written declaration from the client confirming non-resident status and offshore end-use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form CED-1) filed via the Samoa Customs electronic single window for any physical deliverable (e.g., mastered media, subtitling files on physical media)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export (where goods/media are shipped internationally)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Conversion Record issued by a licensed Samoan bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Signed international service contract between the IC and the non-resident client
Digital delivery evidence (upload/download logs, e-mail transmittals, server log extracts, content delivery network reports) for fully electronic localization deliverables
Client acceptance certificate or end-client confirmation of offshore use of the localized media
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA conducts risk-based audits of zero-rated export claims for translation and digital media services, scrutinizing the nexus between the contracted service, the offshore recipient, and the remittance trail. Under the Tax Administration Act 2012, incorrect zero-rating claims attract a shortfall penalty of 25% for failure to take reasonable care, 75% for reckless behavior, 150% for intentional or fraudulent evasion, plus a late-payment penalty of 2% per month (capped at 150% of the unpaid VAGST). The Commissioner may retrospectively claw back refunds and adjust assessments within four years of the assessment date (unlimited in cases of fraud or willful misrepresentation). Criminal prosecution for tax evasion carries fines up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to seven years; directors, officers, and the registered agent are jointly and severally liable where the exporter knowingly supplies false or misleading export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; exercises exchange control under the Exchange Control Act 1974 and Exchange Control Regulations 1985, with delegated supervision of Authorized Dealers and the Financial Intelligence Unit for AML/CFT matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is convertible for bona fide current-account items through Authorized Dealers, but the capital account is regulated: outward capital transfers by residents require Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) approval. A Samoa International Company (IC) is classified as non-resident for exchange-control purposes and may hold foreign-currency accounts without surrender obligations; however, any WST-denominated transaction touching a Samoa resident (e.g., local contractors or onshore overhead paid into Tala accounts) is exchange-controlled and requires a CBS declaration or prior approval. Profit remittance by the IC is free of income tax and without non-resident withholding, but must be executed through the IC's designated foreign-currency account to avoid onshore conversion constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters must collect full invoice proceeds within the six-month statutory window prescribed under the Exchange Control Act 1974 and credit them to an Authorized Dealer; absent a CBS retention limit, proceeds must be converted into WST. The IC, as a non-resident exporter of professional localization services, is exempt from the surrender and conversion obligation; invoiced USD/EUR/AUD receipts for translation and media-dubbing services may be retained indefinitely in its approved foreign-currency account, with the bank reporting year-end balances to the CBS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency corporate account (USD/EUR/AUD) and Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for IC treasury settlement
Offshore International Company USD savings/transaction account with SWIFT USD clearing and trade finance desk
Domestic corporate operating account (WST) plus foreign-currency account
Corporate FCY account; primarily domestic payroll and clearing services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW-MEDIUM feasibility rating for Wise B2B and Payoneer. Neither entity is licensed by the Central Bank of Samoa; they operate as offshore e-money and payout aggregators. Legal constraints: (i) the IC may lawfully hold offshore e-money balances; (ii) repatriation to a Samoa FCA is treated as an inbound remittance requiring source-of-funds evidence; (iii) EMIs cannot directly debit a local WST clearing account, so contractor payments must be made to offshore recipients; (iv) the IC should maintain a licensed Authorized Dealer account as the master treasury vault and use EMI rails only for small-batch outbound contractor payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the CBS AML/CFT Directive and most banks mandate a physical onboarding interview for the beneficial owner and at least one director when opening an IC account. Relaxation is available through a SIFA-licensed registered agent introducer, with notarized and apostilled board resolutions plus certified passport copies accepted as remote documents. Fully remote video onboarding is permissible only where the bank concludes enhanced due diligence and obtains a bank reference from the entity's home-state bank; otherwise, a one-business-day in-person visit to the bank's Apia branch is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt IC status with zero onshore substance (registered-office only) screened as potential shell or brass-plate risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; SIFA registered-agent appointment letter; IC register extracts showing issued shares; client service agreements and localization project register; translation and dubbing delivery evidence; beneficial-ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ownership - nominee shareholders, historical bearer-share flags, or sanctions screening hits on UBO names.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO register filed with SIFA; passport and proof-of-address for each beneficial owner; sworn declaration confirming no bearer warrants outstanding; negative sanctions and disqualification search results; introducer's regulatory reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value cross-border settlements from online payment platforms in FATF-monitored jurisdictions (typical localization receivables).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Wise/Payoneer monthly payout statements; matching invoices and statements of work; delivery metadata and translation-memory audit trails; written AML risk-tier assessment confirming Low_Risk_Standard classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lumpy vendor disbursements to foreign freelance contractors inconsistent with stated headcount or routed to tax-haven jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor KYC pack per contractor; executed master services agreements; freelancer onboarding and payment schedule; source-of-funds evidence for payments above the CBS large-transaction threshold; internal compliance sign-off memorandum.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route: foreign shareholder bank sends SWIFT MT103 credit to the IC's USD-denominated FCA held at BSP or ANZ Samoa. Field 70 description must state 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - WS_IC - INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES ACT 1987'. Samoa does not enforce a formal BOP purpose-code taxonomy, but the authorized dealer's exchange-control section requires a board resolution, updated share register, and funds-source statement for amounts above the CBS reporting threshold. Funds are freely deployable while maintained in foreign currency; conversion into WST requires Authorized Dealer pricing and, if paid onward to a Samoan resident, a CBS exchange-control application.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103 single credit transfers debiting the IC's FCA for contractor and vendor settlements; SWIFT MT202 for interbank nodal transfers through the bank's correspondent network (e.g., ANZ in Australia or BSP in Fiji). Commercial letters of credit are not applicable to pure services; a standby LC or bank guarantee in USD may be issued by the clearing bank for media-dubbing delivery milestones. Wise B2B and Payoneer batch payouts are permissible for sub-USD 10,000 contractor payments, funded from the local FCA, keeping FCY debits entirely offshore and avoiding WST conversion approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Authorized-Dealer deliverable USD/WST forward contracts (maximum 12-month tenor) against committed service-invoice receivables; speculative uncovered positions prohibited.
Offshore USD/WST non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for net WST-position hedging, with cash settlement referenced to the official CBS indicative rate.
Natural hedging via multi-currency FCA concentration accounts (USD/EUR/AUD) requiring zero FX conversion, with periodic inter-currency sweeps executed at Authorized Dealer margin.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) available only under explicit CBS approval for documented commercial exposure; in practice, rolling forward contracts are the accepted substitute.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee (International Company License Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; payment due within 30 days after anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge per month or part thereof, cumulative up to 50% of the unpaid fee; continued non-payment may lead to administrative strike-off after 6 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of USD 200; persistent default triggers restoration order and may result in deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies (Beneficial Ownership Register), MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed simultaneously with the annual return; any change in beneficial ownership due to share transfer must be reported within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 10,000 for false or late submissions; directors may face personal liability and disqualification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a tax-exempt International Company under the International Companies Act 1987. An audit may be required if the company is licensed to provide financial services, expressly mandated by its constitution, or ordered by the Registrar for regulatory investigation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutorily imposed accounting framework for exempt International Companies; records must accurately reflect transactions and financial position. If a voluntary audit is performed, IFRS is generally applied.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2020, each International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office and file an annual confirmation of beneficial ownership together with the annual return. Any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be declared to the Registrar within 14 days of the transfer being registered in the company's own register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 per annum for registered office and resident registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per engagement if a voluntary independent audit is commissioned; no statutory audit fee is normally incurred

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (standard resident company rate under the Income Tax Ordinance 1974, as amended); International Companies (ICs) benefit from a statutory 0% rate on all foreign-source income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IC statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 2009 s.219: 0% income tax on profits derived outside Samoa; no capital gains tax on share disposals; optional full loss ring-fencing with 5-year carryforward for any future domestic taxable activities; annual government fee (renewal fee) substitutes all income tax filing obligations while exempt status is maintained

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return / Annual Renewal Certificate (International Companies Act 2009, Schedule 2 Form) filed through the Samoa Companies Online Registry administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) at www.companies.gov.ws
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the registration anniversary date of incorporation each year; pro-rated fee charged for newly incorporated entities; a 60-day late renewal grace is not statutory and reinstatement requires a formal application after the registrable date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and unique Registration Number (CRN)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact English/Chinese name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; no transliteration changes permitted without prior MCIL approval
Must be the physical office of the licensed registered agent; a PO Box alone is insufficient and may trigger compliance review

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Agent name and licence number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Samoan-licensed agent acts as the primary regulatory contact; foreign directors must ensure the agent holds an active International Company Management Licence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors details: full legal names, nationality, residential address, date of birth
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; provide a serviceable address and valid passport copy; any change must be notified within 30 days

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders and issued share capital: names, share classes, number of shares and consideration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; disclose beneficial owners for AML purposes; nominee holdings must be supported by an express trust declaration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company Secretary (if appointed) and its licensed status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A secretary is optional but must be a Samoa-licensed corporate services provider if named; foreign corporate secretaries are not recognised

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual declaration that the company has not carried on business in Samoa and has derived no Samoan-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the critical tax-exemption safeguard; any domestic activity (physical office, local employees, Samoan clients) invalidates the declaration and triggers the 27% domestic CIT

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance statement: principal place of business and nature of activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a multilingual translation/transcreation IC, confirm that management decisions, servers, and operational staff are located outside Samoa; inadequate substance invites offshore-company scrutiny

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late renewal surcharge of WST 250 per month; automatic strike-off after 6 months without renewal; restoration fee WST 500 plus all arrears; deregistration without prejudice to civil liability of directors for debts incurred while the company was non-compliant

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR1 Company Income Tax Return (only if IC loses statutory exemption) filed via the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) e-filing system (tax.gov.ws)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after the fiscal year-end (standard fiscal year: 31 December); quarterly installments of estimated tax are payable on 15 May, 15 August, 15 November and 15 February

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income from Samoan-source activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the source rules under the Income Tax Ordinance; revenue from centralized localization services delivered to non-resident clients is foreign-source and excluded

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: rent, staff, subcontracted translators, software amortization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility requires onshore economic activity; intercompany payments to the foreign parent must satisfy the arm's length standard
No deemed-rate relief or IC exemption applies once the company admits Samoan-source income; immediate reassessment for previous open years is likely

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due per month up to 25%; interest at 1.5% per month on unpaid tax; evasion penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall on deliberate misdeclaration

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders (IC dividends are outside the Samoan WHT net); domestic statutory rate of 15% applies only where the paying company derives Samoan-source income
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's DTA network is minimal and no comprehensive treaty ordinarily applies to IC dividend flows; where relief is theoretically available the protocol is: (1) obtain a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate via the SRA; (2) submit a Treaty Relief Application Form (WHT-T) with the dividend resolution, share register extract, and foreign tax authority TRC; (3) SRA adjudication within 14 working days; (4) apply reduced WHT at payment source or claim a refund within 3 years of the payment date. For ICs, the recommended route is simply to preserve the 0% exemption and avoid Samoan-source payments
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT to non-residents: interest 15%, royalties 15%; treaty rates are unavailable in the standard IC structure. An IC paying cross-border royalties for subtitling software or interest on shareholder loans suffers no Samoan WHT on the pay-out side; conversely, an IC receiving Samoan-source licence fees is subject to 15% WHT and must maintain an exemption certificate to avoid leakage. Loans must carry arm's length interest and adequate documentation to prevent thin-capitalization and recharacterization

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 0 - Samoa has no codified Local File or Master File thresholds; contemporaneous benchmarking is nonetheless recommended for any related-party cross-border flows exceeding WST 1,000,000 equivalent, and the SRA may request documentation on audit under the general anti-avoidance provisions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applies through the International Companies Act 2009 s.219 and MCIL administrative policy: the IC must not carry on business in Samoa and must demonstrate real economic substance in its outside-Samoa operations. For a localization agency this means foreign-office premises, foreign employed linguists/dubbing staff, foreign-controlled bank accounts (Wise/Payoneer), and client-facing substance overseas. Failure to maintain the declaration of non-domestic business triggers withdrawal of exempt status, full 27% taxation, and adverse treatment as a tax haven shell

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Domestic Business Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An IC operating a translation/transcreation business through Samoan premises or staffing a local production studio while declaring no Samoan-source income on the Annual Return, thereby denying the 27% domestic CIT and evading WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive assessment for up to 5 open years; 150% evasion penalty on the tax shortfall; monthly interest at 1.5%; deregistration of the IC; publication of the company and directors on the SRA defaulters list
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal civil restitution for taxes and penalties; travel bans and exit controls under the Tax Administration Act; imprisonment up to 7 years for wilful evasion; disqualification as directors of any Samoa company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal IC with no foreign operational substance, no foreign staff, and no independent commercial activity, used solely as a pass-through for royalty and dubbing fee income while the real business is managed and executed in Samoa
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off and forfeiture of assets to the Crown upon deregistration; loss of limited-liability protection; fines up to WST 100,000 under the International Companies Act 2009; refusal of the annual renewal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil for all company debts; directors liable to creditors for contracts entered during the non-compliant period; exclusion from future Samoan licence schemes; travel bans pending investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting settlement proceeds through Wise_B2B or Payoneer in the IC's name for localization services without maintaining customer due diligence records, without beneficial ownership identification, or without filing a Suspicious Transaction Report when proceeds display high-risk patterns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to WST 500,000 for the corporate body; freezing orders over all bank and payment-rail balances; mandatory cancellation of the IC registration; reporting to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent are jointly and severally liable for AML penalties if involved in the breach; imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering; restraint orders and travel bans during the investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mispricing intercompany translation, dubbing, and licencing transactions between the Samoa IC and a related non-resident group entity, or funding the IC with excessive shareholder loans at non-arm's length interest, to shift profit artificially to a lower-tax jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment on arms's length terms; a 25% substantial-valuation penalty on any TP adjustment exceeding WST 50,000; denial of interest deductions for excessive debt; potential criminal referral if conduct is fraudulent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved the transfer pricing documentation face joint liability for the deficiency if the IC is struck off; civil claims by minority shareholders; professional disqualification in Samoa and treaty-partner jurisdictions
